solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Detectives on Roman force thick and tenacious (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, a piece placed on another comes after it, so CID follows VIS

blocks.note: vis is the Latin word for force
CID = Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

annotation.surface: A police procedural set in ancient Rome, with detectives joining a tough, dogged legion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roman force' suggests a legion or the Roman police; it wants the Latin word for force itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Viscid describes something sticky and glutinous, so thick and tenacious in the way treacle clings.

entries.clue: Tiny hole in tank terminal for that old canal boat (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the tiny hole sits inside the tank
indicatorNotes.terminal for: the terminal of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a vat is a large tank, here split VA…T around the hole
a pore is a tiny opening in the skin
the last letter of thaT
O = old, a standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A leaky old narrowboat whose water tank has sprung a tiny hole.
annotation.walkthrough: The canal in question is Venetian: a vaporetto is the water-bus of Venice. Note 'that old' is not a phrase; T comes from 'that' and O from 'old'.
annotation.definitionFit: A vaporetto is the motor boat that serves as public transport on the canals of Venice.

entries.clue: Venerable Hindu perhaps crawled over India (5)

blocks.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke, so to have crawled is to have swum
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: An aged holy man inching his way across India on hands and knees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crawled' pictures creeping on all fours; it is the swimming stroke. 'Over' in a down clue simply puts SWAM on top of I.
annotation.definitionFit: Swami is a title of respect for a Hindu religious teacher, so a venerable Hindu, 'perhaps' because not every such person is one.

entries.clue: Wonky line cut by fine horse unsuited to ploughing (8)

indicatorNotes.Wonky: wonky means crooked, so the letters of LINE go askew
indicatorNotes.cut by: the horse cuts into the rearranged line, splitting it in two

blocks.note: LINE rearranged, then split IN…LE
the Arab is a prized breed of horse

annotation.surface: A crooked furrow ruined by a thoroughbred that was never meant to pull a plough.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is just praise for the horse, not a separate instruction; the Arab is a noble breed, which is why it is no plough horse.
annotation.definitionFit: Arable land can be ploughed and farmed, so inarable land is unsuited to ploughing.

entries.clue: Spotted smoked ham was in the van (8)

blocks.note: speck is a smoked ham from the Tyrol
to be in the van (vanguard) is to be at the front, leading

annotation.surface: A deli delivery: someone saw a smoked ham riding in the delivery van.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like the verb 'saw' opening a sighting; it is the adjective. 'The van' is the vanguard, not a vehicle.
annotation.definitionFit: Speckled means marked with small spots.

entries.clue: Sit around drunk at four, late out of theatre (4-9)

indicatorNotes.around: POSE goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose; split POS…E
a toper is a heavy drinker
used as it stands
Roman numeral four

annotation.surface: A drinker still propping up the bar at four, far too late to leave the theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: The theatre is an operating theatre, not a playhouse; 'late out of' means lately out of, just after surgery.
annotation.definitionFit: Post-operative describes the period just after an operation, when a patient is newly out of the operating theatre.

entries.clue: Conservative begins Hard Times (6)

blocks.note: C = Conservative, the British party
rises = begins, as a river or a day does

annotation.surface: A Tory reading Dickens: a Conservative starts on Hard Times.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make 'Hard Times' the Dickens novel; the definition wants the plain words, times of hardship.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym once the capitals are ignored: a crisis is a spell of acute difficulty or danger.

entries.clue: Fancy something strong to drink quickly (4,1,4)

blocks.note: to fancy something is to like it
a shot is a small measure of spirits

annotation.surface: Someone at the bar tempted to knock back a stiff drink in one go.
annotation.walkthrough: The drinking picture sets up 'quickly' as how the drink goes down, but it is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: To do something like a shot is to do it instantly and eagerly.

entries.clue: Divine young woman in towel commercial (5)

blocks.note: to towel something is to dry it
an ad is a commercial

annotation.surface: A gorgeous model in a TV advert for towels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Divine' reads as 'gorgeous' and describes the model; it means literally divine, a minor goddess.
annotation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph of Greek myth, a young female spirit of divine nature.

entries.clue: Notice young man secures vehicle after parking (7)

indicatorNotes.secures: the young man holds the vehicle inside him
indicatorNotes.after: the car-in-lad unit comes after parking, so P is written first

blocks.note: P = parking, as on road signs
a lad is a young man; split LA…D
a car is a vehicle

annotation.surface: A notice that a young man locks up his car after parking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After parking' puts P first even though it comes last in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A placard is a sign or poster displayed as a public notice.

entries.clue: Panic spread beginning in economy, a turbulent flight? (13)

indicatorNotes.beginning in: the beginning of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.turbulent: turbulent means churned up, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the first letter of Economy
used as it stands, the last of the fodder

annotation.surface: A nervous passenger in economy class panicking on a bumpy flight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flight' is set up as a plane journey by 'economy' and 'turbulent'; it means running away. The question mark flags that twist.
annotation.definitionFit: Flight is fleeing, and fleeing makes someone vanish: a disappearance.

entries.clue: Last of runners flash past — don’t give up (5,2)

blocks.note: the last letter of runnerS
a tick and a flash both mean an instant
to go past is to go by

annotation.surface: Encouragement to the tail-ender in a race as the leaders flash past.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like a verb of speed next to 'runners'; it is the noun, a moment, as in 'back in a tick'.
annotation.definitionFit: To stick by someone is to stay loyal and not give up on them.

entries.clue: Indian side cheers on attack that lacks depth (5)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, 'on' puts the first piece after the second
indicatorNotes.that lacks depth: to lack something is to be without it, and depth abbreviates to D, so RAID loses its D

blocks.note: RAID without D (depth)
ta is British slang for thanks, and cheers means thanks

annotation.surface: A cricket report: the Indian team cheers an attack lacking depth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Indian side' sounds like a cricket team; it is a side dish. Raita is the yogurt and cucumber accompaniment to a curry.
annotation.definitionFit: Raita is a yogurt dish served on the side with Indian food.

entries.clue: Cannonball shortly due to land (9)

indicatorNotes.shortly: the word is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: SHOT, a cannonball, cut short
one's due is what one deserves, a reward

annotation.surface: A cannonball about to come down on land any moment now.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shortly due' looks like 'expected soon'; 'shortly' belongs to the cannonball, and 'due' is a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Shoreward means towards the shore, in the direction of land.

entries.clue: Ship leaves once loaded (3,7)

blocks.note: the surface reading: a ship departs; the meant reading: a ship's cargo of (tea) leaves
the surface reading: as soon as it is loaded; the meant reading: formerly laden, with that cargo

annotation.surface: A ship setting sail as soon as its cargo is aboard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as the verb 'departs'; it is the noun, tea leaves, which the ship once carried as cargo. 'Once' points to its nineteenth-century heyday.
annotation.definitionFit: A tea clipper was a fast sailing ship that carried tea from China to Britain in the nineteenth century.

entries.clue: A bit of skin cook sliced off sounds attractive (9)

indicatorNotes.sounds: it is the sound of the phrase that gives the answer

blocks.clueFragment: A bit of skin cook sliced off
blocks.note: a peeling is a strip of skin pared off a vegetable

annotation.surface: A cook who has sliced off a bit of their finger, not an attractive sight.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a kitchen injury; the skin is a vegetable's, and 'a peeling' said aloud is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something appealing draws you towards it.

entries.clue: High street business, can it work? (4)

blocks.note: 'can it!' means 'be quiet!', which is sh
op = opus, a work

annotation.surface: A worried owner wondering whether a high street business can be made to pay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can it work?' reads as a question about viability; 'can it' is slang for shut up. A high street is a town's main shopping street.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: retail premises are the typical high street business, alongside banks and cafés.

entries.clue: Sphinxlike features Oscar saw cut in step (5,4)

indicatorNotes.in: O and KERF go inside PACE

blocks.note: a pace is a step; split P…ACE
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a kerf is the slit made by a saw

annotation.surface: Oscar watching an enigmatic statue being sawn apart in step, face giving nothing away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of 'see', with Oscar watching; it is the tool, and the cut it makes has its own name, kerf.
annotation.definitionFit: The Sphinx is famously inscrutable, and a poker face is an expression that gives nothing away.

entries.clue: Round of applause a little generous (8)

blocks.note: to give someone a hand is to applaud them
some = a little

annotation.surface: An audience grudging with its applause, which was only a little generous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Handsome' is used here in its sense of ample, as in a handsome tip, not good-looking.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense of the word: a handsome tip or offer is liberal in amount, nothing to do with looks.

entries.clue: Only two-thirds of cutlery put back, oh dear (4)

indicatorNotes.Only two-thirds of: keep four of the six letters

blocks.note: SPOONS, a kind of cutlery, trimmed to its first four of six letters

annotation.surface: Someone clearing up finds only two-thirds of the cutlery was returned to the drawer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cutlery' has to become a specific six-letter item before two-thirds of it can be taken; SPOONS gives SPOO.
annotation.definitionFit: Oops is the exclamation of someone who has just made a small blunder, like oh dear.

entries.clue: 20C composer’s babel developed technique, all right (4,6)

indicatorNotes.developed: the letters of babel are worked into a new shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder
an art is a skill or technique
OK = all right

annotation.surface: A critic grudgingly admitting that a modern composer's din has a sound technique.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Babel' reads as a racket of discordant music; it is only letters. 20C is the twentieth century.
annotation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer of the twentieth century.

entries.clue: Monster logically following that capsized ship (6)

indicatorNotes.capsized: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue the word is turned over

blocks.note: ergo = therefore, what logically follows
SS = steamship

annotation.surface: A monster following a ship that has overturned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capsized' seems to belong to the ship; it acts on ERGO. The definition is looser than the answer, since an ogress is a female ogre.
annotation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a man-eating monster of folklore.

entries.clue: NZ city with large aviation facility that is in recession (9)

indicatorNotes.in recession: receding means going backwards, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: w = with, as in w/
a hangar houses aircraft
i.e. = that is

annotation.surface: A New Zealand city with a big airport hangar at a time of economic downturn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In recession' looks like economic news; it turns IE round. Whangarei is a city in the far north of New Zealand's North Island.
annotation.definitionFit: Whangarei is a city in Northland, New Zealand.

entries.clue: What rambler does having lost new waterproof boot (5)

indicatorNotes.having lost: what the rambler does has lost something, so a letter comes out of WANDER

blocks.note: a rambler wanders
N = new, removed from WANDER

annotation.surface: A hiker who has lost a new waterproof boot.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a hiker's mishap; 'having lost new' is the instruction to drop N from WANDER.
annotation.definitionFit: A wader is a high waterproof boot worn for standing in water.

entries.clue: Celebration instead of defeat (2,3)

blocks.note: a do is a party
as in 'swap this for that'

annotation.surface: A party held in place of a loss.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets celebration against defeat as opposites; 'defeat' is the definition, and 'do for' is informal for finish off.
annotation.definitionFit: To do for someone is to ruin or finish them off, to defeat them.

entries.clue: Female dressing, a stone lighter (5)

blocks.note: F = female
lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds

annotation.surface: A woman in a wound dressing, now a stone lighter after dieting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A stone lighter' reads as weight lost; it is a stone that lights, the flint struck to make a spark.
annotation.definitionFit: Flint is a hard stone that sparks when struck, used as the lighter in cigarette lighters.

entries.clue: Blood vessel opened by doctor, one showing concern for the motorist (5-2)

indicatorNotes.opened by: DR and I open the word, standing in front of VEIN

blocks.note: Dr = doctor
I = one, the Roman numeral
a vein is a blood vessel

annotation.surface: A doctor opening a vein, a caring medic attending a motorist after a crash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Showing' and 'concern' suggest care; a drive-in is a business, especially a cinema, showing films to people in their cars.
annotation.definitionFit: A drive-in cinema is one showing films to motorists, a concern (business) for them.

entries.clue: Adult works at aerobics, desperately wanting shaped abs (7)

indicatorNotes.desperately: done desperately, the letters are thrown about
indicatorNotes.wanting: wanting means lacking, so ABS is removed

blocks.note: used as it stands, part of the fodder
AEROBICS without the letters A, B, S

annotation.surface: An adult working out at aerobics, desperate for a sculpted six-pack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Adult works' passes for a grown-up who exercises; it is adult material. 'Shaped' makes the removed letters form ABS in any order.
annotation.definitionFit: Erotica are literary or artistic works of a sexual nature, adult works.

entries.clue: Roll touching substance that’s dubious (8)

blocks.note: re = regarding, touching on
the gist is the substance of a matter
er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

annotation.surface: A bread roll that has been handled by some questionable stuff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roll' reads as bread; it is a roll of names, as in a roll call.
annotation.definitionFit: A roll is an official list of names, a register.

entries.clue: Little Scottish collars its, on reflection? (6)

annotation.definition: Little Scottish collars its, on reflection?

indicatorNotes.collars: WEE goes round the other letters like a collar
indicatorNotes.on reflection: a reflection is reversed, so ITS turns round

blocks.note: wee is Scots for little; split WE…E
ITS reversed

annotation.surface: A small Scottish dog regarding its own collar in a mirror.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a westie is a little Scottish dog, and dogs wear collars. The question mark flags that double duty.
annotation.definitionFit: A westie is a West Highland white terrier, a small Scottish breed that wears a collar like any dog.
